column1: Beginning in 1973 policymakers had to cope with the large supply shocks caused by OPEC. OPEC first raised oil prices in the mid-1970s, pushing the inflation rate above 9 percent. This adverse supply shock, together with temporarily tight monetary policy, led to a recession in 1975. High unemployment during the recession reduced inflation somewhat, but further OPEC price hikes pushed inflation up again in the late 1970s.
